case_name: Burada Kanaka Ratnam vs Senior Superintendent Of Posts And Ors.

parties.respondent_defendant: Senior Superintendent Of Posts And Ors.

facts_of_case: Petitioner was a widow who underwent training to become a Postal Assistant. She was discharged from the training without notice and was orally threatened with arrest if she did not credit an amount paid towards her stipend. The petitioner claims that this discharge is illegal and in violation of principles of natural justice.

legal_principles.principle: Unless there is clear proof of re-marriage, the status as a widow continues.
legal_principles.held: The learned Counsel would contend that absolutely there is no proof of re-marriage and unless there is clear proof of re-marriage, the writ petitioner won't cease to be a widow

legal_principles.principle: Courts of law are expected to enforce the provisions of law.
legal_principles.held: The learned Counsel also would submit that the Courts of law are expected to enforce the provisions of law and unless the respondents are able to show any specific legal bar in this regard, the discharge is illegal

legal_principles.principle: The mere fact that the writ petitioner begot a child by living with someone does not alter her status as a widow.
legal_principles.held: The learned Counsel also would maintain that no specific statutory provision or service rule or regulation had been shown that on the ground of unchastity or on the ground on which the writ petitioner had been disqualified the writ petitioner would cease to be a widow

legal_principles.principle: Unless a specific legal bar is shown, the discharge is illegal.
legal_principles.held: The learned Counsel also would submit that unless the respondents are able to show any specific legal bar in this regard, the discharge is illegal

outcome.final_order: The court issued a writ of certiorari calling for records in O.A. No. 1713/98 on the file of Central Administrative Tribunal, Hyderabad, and quashed the said order.

guiding a client on the process of appointment and discharge as a Postal Assistant
